meta.title: NCI Student Information Assistant
meta.audience: Postgraduate (MSc) students at National College of Ireland
meta.disclaimer: This assistant only returns answers that are written down in this knowledge base. Every answer is taken from the public NCI website and links to the official page. If it cannot find a confident match it says so and points you to NCI directly. It never guesses.
meta.privacy: No personal data is collected or displayed. Nothing about individual students or staff is stored here.

fallback.message: I could not find a confident answer to that in my knowledge base, so I am not going to guess. Here are the official NCI pages where this is answered:

entries.question: What are the start and end dates of the semester?
variants: When does the semester start and finish?
when do classes begin and end
entries.answer: For 2026/27, Semester 1 classes run Monday 14 September 2026 to Saturday 12 December 2026. Semester 2 runs Monday 18 January 2027 to Saturday 24 April 2027. Semester 3 (May to August) runs Monday 17 May 2027 to Saturday 7 August 2027. NCI runs its academic year from September to August. If you started in January 2027 your Semester 1 is 18 January to 24 April 2027. Check the academic calendar regularly because dates are indicative and can change.

entries.question: When does reading week start?
entries.answer: Semester 1 reading week is Monday 26 October to Saturday 31 October 2026, with no classes and no new Springboard or ICT Skillnet sessions. Semester 2 reading week is Monday 15 March to Saturday 20 March 2027, also with no classes. Saturday classes resume the following day. Note that Monday 26 October 2026 is the October Bank Holiday, so NCI is closed that day. The calendar is indicative and can change, so check the page before you plan around it.

entries.question: When is my assignment due?
variants: What is the deadline for my assignment?
entries.answer: Assignment due dates are set per module, so there is no single college-wide deadline. The authoritative date is the one in your assignment brief on the module page in Moodle, together with the module descriptor. A small number of MSc programmes run a dissertation or project in the June to August period with a submission due in August, so check your programme handbook as well. I cannot see module briefs from here, so please read the brief on Moodle.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Moodle (module page for your brief)

entries.question: Which referencing style should I use?
variants: What is the referencing style used at NCI?
how do I cite sources in my assignment
entries.answer: NCI uses three referencing styles. Harvard is the most widely used, across most School of Business courses and some School of Computing modules. APA is used by Psychology, Education and Learning and Teaching students. IEEE is used in some School of Computing modules. Harvard is an author-date system: you put a short (Author, Year) citation in the text and a full reference in a list titled References, in alphabetical order by author surname and with no numbering. Every in-text citation must match a reference list entry and vice versa. Always confirm the exact style your module requires with your lecturer.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Referencing and Avoiding Plagiarism guide

entries.question: When and where is my exam this semester?
variants: where do I sit my exam?
is my exam online or on campus
entries.answer: Exams run in three main periods each year. For 2026/27 they are Semester 1 from 5 to 16 January 2027, Semester 2 from 4 to 22 May 2027, and Semester 3 and repeat exams from 3 to 21 August 2027. Each exam takes place either on the Mayor Square campus in NCI or on Moodle, and the location is decided per paper rather than for the whole session. Morning, afternoon and evening sessions are all used, so check your programme's timetable carefully for the exact date, time and room. You cannot request a change of exam date or time, and alternative arrangements are not available, so attend the location shown on the timetable.

entries.question: What is the required word count for my assignment?
variants: how many words does my assignment need
how long should my assignment be
entries.answer: There is no college-wide word count. Each module sets its own word count and assessment weighting, so the number you must meet is the one in your assignment brief on Moodle and in the module descriptor. Some published examples: the BA (Hons) Psychology final year project dissertation runs 6,000 to 8,000 words, and Level 9 dissertations follow the specification in the Postgraduate Dissertation Handbook for your school. I am not going to invent a number for your module, so please check the brief.

entries.question: How do I apply for an assignment extension?
variants: how do I get more time for my assignment
I need an extension on my deadline
how do I ask for a re-run
entries.answer: Extensions and re-runs are requested through NCI360, not by email to your lecturer. Log in to NCI360, choose Key Application Forms and Requests, then select Application for Coursework Extension/Rerun. You must state the module affected, the assessment format, the period of time affected and the grounds for the application, and you must attach supporting documentation such as a medical certificate, or the request cannot be processed. Apply at least two days before the submission deadline. Extensions are only granted in exceptional circumstances and cannot be granted for Terminal Alternative Assessments or for the 4th Year Software Project module, and your programme co-ordinator will tell you if the QQI exam board dates make an extension impossible.

entries.question: How do I resit an exam?
variants: how do I repeat an exam
what happens if I fail an exam
entries.answer: If you defer an assessment or exam, it is normally completed at the next sitting or repeat session for that module in the same academic year. For 2026/27 the repeat and Semester 3 exam period is 3 to 21 August 2027, and there is a further Semester 3 and repeat exam period from 5 to 21 January 2028 for the September 2027 starters. These dates come from the Academic Calendar rather than the deferrals page. Be aware that NCI distinguishes three kinds of deferral: an assessment deferral is completed at the next sitting, but a module or programme deferral moves you to the following academic year, so check which type you have been granted. Deferral requests are submitted through NCI360 and the normal turnaround is ten working days, so apply well before the exam.

entries.question: When will my exam results be released?
variants: how long until I get my grades
entries.answer: Results are published after each exam session has concluded, and you check them by logging in to the MyDetails area once the published date for your session has passed. The most recently published dates were for Semester 3 2025/26: for PGD and Masters programmes results went live on MyDetails on 25 September 2026, the deadline for Review and Recheck forms was 1 October 2026, and exam reviews took place on 5 October 2026. Undergraduate programmes were 9 September 2026, with rechecks by 11 September and reviews on 15 September 2026. NCI states these dates are provisional and subject to change, and reviews are for completed programmes only, so always take the exact date for your session from the Exam Results Information page.

entries.question: Who is my programme co-ordinator?
variants: who should I talk to about my course
entries.answer: NCI says your programme co-ordinator's details are on your course page in Moodle, so check there first. To contact them, submit a request to Academic Operations through the NCI Support Hub, and it is routed automatically to the right programme co-ordinator. Academic Operations also manage the day-to-day of your programme. I deliberately do not store staff names or any personal details in this assistant, so please use the official routes above to get the current, correct person for your programme.

entries.question: How do I access Moodle?
variants: how do I get into moodle
entries.answer: Go to https://moodle2026.ncirl.ie/ and sign in with Single Sign On using the same NCI credentials you use everywhere else: your username in the format x12345678@student.ncirl.ie and your NCI password. The same credentials also work for MyDetails, Office 365, Wi-Fi and the virtual desktop, so you only ever have one password. If you cannot log in, reset it first at https://password.ncirl.ie/ , and if the account is locked after too many wrong attempts, the Password Management service will unlock it as well.

entries.question: Where do I find my lecture material?
entries.answer: Lecture slides, notes, readings and recordings are published on your module page in Moodle, usually in the section for that week. If something is not on the module page, ask your lecturer, as material is sometimes distributed in class only. The formal description of each module, including learning outcomes and assessment weighting, is in the NCI module descriptors at http://courses.ncirl.ie/index.cfm , and the library has subject and module guides for finding readings at https://libguides.ncirl.ie/subjectandlibraryguides . I cannot read your private module pages, so the brief and materials are best found in Moodle.

entries.question: How do I submit my assignment on Moodle?
entries.answer: Open your module page in Moodle, go to the assessment you are submitting, click the submission link and upload your file. Many assignments are submitted through Turnitin, which is linked from the same page; if your work has security settings or is password protected, remove them before uploading or the file will not open for your marker. You get an automatic submission receipt, so always check that you receive one and check your uploaded file opens correctly. If the upload fails, take a screenshot and contact the module lecturer or Student Services the same day. I cannot see the per-module upload link, so please use the one in your Moodle module page.

entries.question: How do I register for my seat for the new year?
variants: how do I pay my fees to register
how do I confirm my place
entries.answer: Online registration for returning full-time and part-time students opens in July 2026. Registration is done by paying your fees through MyDetails: sign in to the MyApps portal at https://myapps.microsoft.com/ with your NCI credentials (x12345678@student.ncirl.ie) and open the myDetails app. You must have paid the required amount before the date of your first class, or access to college services is affected, meaning you will not be able to log in to online classrooms, borrow books from the library, and a late registration charge will be applied. If you are not in receipt of a SUSI grant you must pay at least 20% of the Student Contribution Fee to register, plus the 80 euro gym fee. Part-time Masters students moving from first to second year are rolled over automatically and will be notified by email. Cash is no longer accepted on campus and American Express is not accepted.

entries.question: How do I request a reference letter from NCI?
variants: how do I get a reference letter
I need proof of my student status
entries.answer: You can self-generate most student letters yourself. Sign in to NCI360 at https://nci360.ncirl.ie/ and use the Student Letter Hub, which gives you a registration or reference letter and a letter that can be used as proof of address. You must be a fully registered student and your home and mailing address must be up to date on MyDetails; if you changed your address today, wait until tomorrow because the system can take up to 24 hours to update. If you need a character or academic reference, email academicoperations@ncirl.ie. Immigration letters are issued by the International Office instead. The Exams Office cannot discuss your results with anyone other than you.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Support Hub: How do I request a letter?

entries.question: How do I access the library online?
entries.answer: Sign in to the library with the same NCI credentials you use for Moodle: click Library Login at https://library.ncirl.ie/account . From there you can search the catalogue, use EBSCO Discovery for journal articles, and reach the A-Z list of databases, e-journals and e-books. Online resources are available 24 hours a day from any location, and the Library Academic Support Centre is at https://libguides.ncirl.ie/libraryacademicsupportcentre if you need help. The Norma Smurfit Library is on the 4th and 5th floors of the Spencer Dock campus.

entries.question: How do I borrow books from the library?
variants: how do I get a library book
do I need a student card to borrow
how long can I keep a book
entries.answer: The Norma Smurfit Library is on the 4th and 5th floors of the Spencer Dock campus. Borrow a book by scanning your student card on one of the self-service machines on either floor, or by asking a member of library staff at the information desk on the 4th floor. As a postgraduate you can borrow 10 items at a time for 4 weeks. You need your student card, which is also how you swipe in at the building gates and how your print credit is connected. If every copy of a book is out, place a reservation from the catalogue; you are emailed to your NCI student email when it arrives and you have 5 working days to collect it from the desk. Returns go in the Book Returns Drop Box in the ground floor lobby or via the self-service machines. Overdue fines are 1 euro per item per day and your account is blocked at 10 euro.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Library: Borrowing and Renewing Books

entries.question: How do I renew a library book?
variants: can I keep the book longer
how do I renew a book I borrowed
entries.answer: You do not normally need to do anything. Books automatically renew for another loan period unless another student has requested the title, in which case you will be emailed at your NCI student email address and asked to bring the item back. You can also renew yourself at any time: log in to your library account at https://library.ncirl.ie/account and click Renew, use the self-service kiosk on the 4th or 5th floor with your student card, ask at the library desk, or email library@ncirl.ie. The library is cashless, so fines can only be paid by debit or credit card.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Library: Borrowing and Renewing Books

entries.question: How much is the tuition fee?
variants: how do I pay my tuition
entries.answer: Course fees differ per programme and per mode of study, and NCI publishes the fee for each course on that course's own page rather than in one table. So the reliable way to get your figure is to open the page for your specific course in the NCI course search, which lists the part-time or full-time fee for that programme, and to check it again each year because fees are revised annually. The Postgraduate Fees page explains how to pay rather than what to pay. If paying in one go is difficult, NCI offers a direct debit plan where you pay 20% of the fees up front and the remainder in equal monthly instalments, with no extra charge. If you are an international student, your fees and funding are covered separately. If you need the figure confirmed for your own programme, Student Services or the Fees and Grants office can give you the exact amount that applies to you.

entries.question: Are there scholarships or financial support available?
entries.answer: Yes. NCI runs a range of scholarships, grants and discounts, and the live list with deadlines and how to apply is on the Scholarships and Discounts page. The postgraduate schemes for September 2026 entry included the Master's Edge Scholarship, which is 25% off a full-time, day-time Masters or Postgraduate Diploma for qualified NCI students and alumni; a full Irish Refugee Council postgraduate scholarship for one candidate; the 30% Club scholarship, which gives two fully funded places, one in the School of Business and Social Sciences and one in the School of Computing; and a 1,000 euro discount for NCI students and alumni. Those deadlines were in May, June and August 2026 and have now passed, so treat them as the pattern rather than as an open application, and check the page for the current round. Note that scholarships cannot be combined, so only the scholarship of highest value is awarded, and that the Master's Edge is daytime only while the 30% Club covers full-time and part-time study. Many of these are not available to students paying international fees, who have a separate scholarship portfolio. Separately from scholarships, if you are in receipt of a SUSI grant you may qualify for the Free Fees Initiative. If money is the barrier to you studying, talk to Student Services about the Student Assistance Fund, the Fund for Students with Disabilities, the emergency hardship fund for international students, and the option of paying by direct debit.

entries.question: What clubs and societies can I join?
variants: how do I join a society
entries.answer: All NCI clubs and societies are run by students, for students, and are free to any registered full-time or part-time student. The current list includes clubs in Football, Basketball, GAA, Ladies GAA, Ladies Basketball, Badminton, Golf, Cricket and Pool/Snooker, and societies including 5 a side, Adventure, African, Arts, Dance, Equality, Fantasy Football, Irish Culture, Mental Health, Movie and Fashion. You sign up through the Students' Union at https://ncisu.ie/clubs-societies/ or at Sign Up Day during Freshers' Week. To start a new society, work with the Clubs and Societies Officer in the Students' Union. You can email clubsandsocs@ncisu.ie or sport@ncirl.ie.

entries.question: When is the orientation programme?
variants: do I have to attend orientation
entries.answer: Orientation takes place before your course starts and covers your programme, the college services and campus life. For part-time and Masters students it is held online in one session via Microsoft Teams, with the date and time for each course listed on the part-time registration and orientation page, and you receive the joining link by email about 48 hours beforehand. Install the Teams app and log in with your NCI username in the format x12345678@student.ncirl.ie. Full-time first years have several in-person sessions in the week before classes begin. All listed dates are indicative and can change. If you cannot attend, email orientation@ncirl.ie.

entries.question: How do I contact the Careers service?
variants: who can help with my CV
entries.answer: The easiest route is email the Careers Team at ncicareersteam@ncirl.ie. The Career Development and Employability Service supports CVs, cover letters, interview technique, online presence and career planning, and you can book an appointment with a Careers Advisor. The team page at https://www.ncirl.ie/Students/Careers/About-Us/Meet-the-Team lists each advisor and the programmes they cover, so you can go straight to the right person. Current students also get free unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning through the MyApps portal.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Career Development and Employability Service

entries.question: What internship or placement opportunities are there?
variants: how do I find an internship
entries.answer: Some MSc programmes include a work placement as a graded part of the degree. The School of Computing placement programmes run for 12 weeks, either May to August or September to December, and include MSc in Cybersecurity, MSc in Artificial Intelligence, MSc in AI for Business, MSc in Data Analytics and MSc in FinTech. On these placements students typically work four days a week in the company and attend class at NCI on the fifth day, so confirm your own pattern with the Careers Team. Whether a placement is a formal credit-bearing part of your programme or something you arrange yourself depends on your course, so check the Courses with Work Placement page for your programme or ask your programme co-ordinator. Independently of that, the NCI online jobs board is updated daily with jobs and placements employers have sent in, and it is accessed from MyApps using your NCI login. Email ncicareersteam@ncirl.ie to talk it through.

entries.question: How do I reset my NCI password?
entries.answer: Go to https://password.ncirl.ie/ and choose the option that fits: Sign up for SSPR to register self-service password reset, Reset Password if you have forgotten it, or Change Password if you know your current one. This is the same password you use for Moodle, MyDetails, Office 365 and Wi-Fi, so resetting it updates everything at once. If you enter it incorrectly several times your IT account is locked, and the Password Management service is also what unlocks it. If you cannot recover it yourself, raise a ticket with IT through the NCI Support Hub at https://ncisupporthub.ncirl.ie/hc/en-ie .

entries.question: How do I connect to NCI Wi-Fi?
entries.answer: Select the network named eduroam on your device and sign in with your NCI credentials: username x12345678@student.ncirl.ie and your NCI password. eduroam is the international research and education roaming network, so the same username and password also work at thousands of other participating universities worldwide, which is useful if you are travelling. On Android 8 or later and on iPhone, the easiest method is to install the free geteduroam app, search for National College of Ireland, choose National College of Ireland IE, then log in and select Join. On Windows set security to WPA2 Enterprise, authentication to PEAP, and the domain to ncirl.ie. If it fails, forget the network on your device to clear any cached password, reset your password, and contact itupport@ncirl.ie if it still will not connect.

entries.question: What free software is available to me?
variants: what apps do I get access to
entries.answer: Your entitlement to software all comes through the MyApps portal at https://myapps.microsoft.com/ . You get Microsoft Office 365 online and you can install the full desktop version of Word, Excel, PowerPoint and the rest on your own device. You also get a Virtual Desktop for software you cannot install locally, free print credit you top up at https://studentprint.ncirl.ie/webcentre/ , and a shared OneDrive and SharePoint. NCI Computing students additionally have access to free developer tools including Visual Studio Community, Visual Studio Code, SQL Server Developer, Visio Professional and Azure services through the Azure Dev Tools for Education link on the MyApps portal. Free online learning is also included, notably LinkedIn Learning.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Support Hub: Getting Started with Online Services

entries.question: How do I book a library study room?
variants: book a room in the library
entries.answer: There are 8 bookable group study rooms in the library, four on the 4th floor (S4.01 for 12 students, S4.12 for 8, S4.13 for 8, S4.08 for 4) and four on the 5th floor (S5.08 for 8, S5.09 for 6, S5.10 for 4, S5.06 for 6). There are two further group rooms on the 1st floor of the Spencer Dock building outside the library, S1.12 for 6 and S1.13 for 8. You book from the study rooms page itself, using the button for the relevant room or the per-room booking links on that page, and you should use your NCI student email address when booking. During the busiest hours of 10am to 4pm Monday to Saturday you must book the room and wait for library staff to approve it, and a booking is not valid until staff approve it, at which point you get an email. Outside those hours you can still book, and you may have to give up the room to someone who booked it. Each room can be booked for a maximum of 2 hours per day per group, most rooms need a minimum of 2 students, and S4.08 and S5.10 can be used by a single student. You must check in within 5 minutes before your start time and within 15 minutes after it, using the link or QR code in your email, on Eduroam. To cancel, use the link in the confirmation email or ask at the desk. There are also four low-distraction desks in the silent study room on the 4th floor for students who find open study distracting.

entries.question: What are the requirements for my MSc dissertation?
variants: when do I submit my dissertation
entries.answer: The dissertation is independent research of your own topic, and the exact requirements are set by your programme's handbook, not by the college as a whole. The minimum requirements for a Level 9 dissertation are published in the Dissertation Submission Specifications and the School of Business Postgraduate Dissertation Handbook, both linked from the library's Thesis and Final Year Project Submission Guide. In summary you submit electronically through Moodle (Turnitin), a hard copy is no longer required, you must complete and sign the Submission of Thesis and Declaration form and attach it, you must turn off any file security before uploading, and an approved electronic copy is then deposited in the library repository NORMA. You are allocated a supervisor. Some programmes set the dissertation due date in August after the taught modules finish, so check your programme handbook and your module page in Moodle. Turnitin also generates the report for checking similarity and AI use, so submit well before the deadline and do not leave generating the report to the last minute.
entries.linkLabel: NCI Library: Thesis and Final Year Project Submission Guide

entries.question: What do I need to do to graduate?
variants: how do I collect my certificate
entries.answer: To be eligible to graduate you must have successfully completed all modules in your programme and your marks must be presented and confirmed at an exam board, be in good standing on fees, and be clear to progress. You cannot move on to the next stage of your programme until every module from the current stage is passed, so an unresolved result blocks graduation. Results are published on MyDetails, and you are emailed when they are available. The next NCI Winter Graduation is on Thursday 22 October 2026 in the Convention Centre Dublin. Tickets cost 65 euro and include gown hire plus entry for two guests, and each student may only buy one. Collect your gown from the Kelly Theatre between 3pm and 7pm on 20 October, or at the Convention Centre up to an hour before your ceremony on the day. All ceremonies are livestreamed. Email graduation@ncirl.ie with any questions, and if you cannot attend, contact the Graduation team about collecting your certificate separately.

entries.question: Where can I find the exam timetable?
entries.answer: The exam timetable is published per programme on the Exam Timetable page, with separate PDF timetables for each exam block. For 2025/26 the published blocks were Semester One 5 to 16 January 2026, Semester Two 5 to 23 May 2026, and Autumn or Repeat 4 to 22 August 2026, with the Sem 2 and August timetables available as PDFs by programme. Exams are either on campus at the Spencer Dock campus or online in Moodle, and the location is shown in the timetable. You must attend the location shown because alternative arrangements are not available. Students are not permitted to request changes to exam dates or times, and the Exams Office may change the timetable, so check it regularly, ideally daily. Full-time and part-time students are expected to sit morning, afternoon and evening sessions.

entries.question: How do I check my exam results?
variants: where can I see my grades
entries.answer: Sign in to MyDetails, which you reach from the MyApps portal, and open the Results section. Your MyDetails shows your overall grade plus a breakdown of each individual module. Current students can also download their results there, and graduating students receive a final transcript by email once their course is complete. If you have completed every module but no overall result is showing, log a ticket with the Exams Office through the NCI Support Hub. If you cannot log in at all and your account is in good standing, use the IT Services guides. If you have outstanding fees your results will be withheld, so contact the Fees Office. If you believe there is an error, raise it with the Exams Office or your programme co-ordinator immediately after publication, as there are fixed deadlines for Recheck (after each results release) and Exam Review (which requires a full set of results for a programme stage). The Exams Office cannot discuss your results with anyone other than you, under data protection law.
